content.content:
19:The command sequence the skills run to format, lint, build, and test before committing or
20:opening a PR. A non-zero exit is a failure the skill must fix before proceeding.
21-
22:**Hard ordering rule:** core (`MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj`) MUST build before the solution or
23-any head. The MGCB content step references `MonoDreams.dll` by absolute path (not as an MSBuild
24-dependency), so the core dll must already exist or the content build fails with
25-`Failed to create importer 'YarnSpinnerImporter'`.
26-
27:- **Full:** `dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj && dotnet test --configuration Release`
28-  - Builds + tests the desktop solution (the `.sln` excludes the web head by design). This is
29-    the required gate.
30-- **Web head (optional — only when the `wasm-tools` workload is installed):**
31:  `dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples.Web/MonoDreams.Examples.Web.csproj -p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web`
32-  - Run this in addition to **Full** when a change touches the `platform` flow or the
33-    rendering/content paths. Install the workload with `dotnet workload install wasm-tools`;
34-    **skip this step entirely if it is not installed** — it hard-fails without the workload and
35-    is deliberately kept out of the core Full gate so Full never fails on a missing workload.
36-- **Incremental** (faster, scoped per-wave — desktop only, skips the heavy web build):
37:  `dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj && dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/`
38-  - Use `dotnet test MonoDreams.Cli.Tests/` instead when the change is CLI-only.
39-- **Always-run gates:** none. The repo ships no format/lint gate (no `.editorconfig`-enforced
40-  style, no architecture tests). Match the surrounding code's style; the codebase's own
41-  consistency is the style guide.
42-
43-## Docs layout
44-
45:Where the docs the skills read and produce live. `{module}` is substituted per change.
46-
47-- **Core tenets:** `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` (engine-wide invariants — read first for any non-trivial change)
48:- **Premises:** `MonoDreams/{module}/docs/premises.md` (**colocated** — per-module technical invariants in Why/Breaks/Tests/Depends-on format)
49-- **Overview** (optional): `MonoDreams/{module}/docs/overview.md` (per-module purpose + wiring tour)
50-- **Schema:** none.
51-- **Planning:** none (no plan-contract spec / recurring-failure-modes docs).

issue #50's four items:

1. TriggerType.Configure + ActiveLayers — the seam that keeps the engine
   clean: a game supplies an optional Action<Entity> hook (and collision
   layers) on its trigger types, so one palette click authors a fully
   functional game object while the module stays ignorant of what it
   built. Empty ActiveLayers = a pure marker (selectable, collides with
   nothing).

2. Undoable Restart — EditorTransport captures the world as SceneData
   before the teardown and pushes ONE RestartUndoCommand onto the
   just-cleared history via the new EditorHistory.PushApplied (record
   without re-applying; refused inside a transaction). Ctrl+Z restores
   the pre-restart world through the reader's sweep/rebuild/restore
   delegates; redo re-runs the reload-from-disk. Exactly one level deep;
   graceful no-push when the snapshot seams aren't wired.

3. Two placement fixes — the active bottom tab joins the palette's
   layout cache key (a programmatic panel:tab switch re-lays the shelf
   instead of leaving Assets chrome painted over the Prefabs tab), and
   drag-stamping gains a per-stroke visited set plus a cross-stroke
   duplicate-cell guard (a wobbling drag never doubles a cell;
   re-clicking a filled cell is a loud-logged no-op).

   PREMULTIPLIED via the lint-blessed Color.Lerp(Transparent, role, a)

input.command:
gh pr create --repo roo-oliv/monodreams --base main --head issue-50 --title "feat(level-editor): fit-and-finish — TriggerType.Configure seam, undoable Restart, placement fixes, grid fade" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes #50

A port of the reference implementation (`roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` → `Gmtk2026.Core/MonoDreams/level-editor/…`), cherry-picked to exactly the issue's four items — the reference repo has since diverged with out-of-scope features (Paint tab / pixel-art wave, layers wave, workspace tabs), none of which ride along here.

## 1. `TriggerType.Configure` + `ActiveLayers` — the seam

`TriggerType` gains two additive init-properties: `Action<Entity>? Configure` (a game hook invoked on the freshly-built trigger entity, after the standard `EntityInfo` + `Transform` + `BoxCollider` stack) and `int[]? ActiveLayers` (scopes the placed box's collision layers; empty = a pure marker that collides with nothing; null = the collider default). `TriggerFactory.Create` applies both. One palette click now authors a fully functional game object while the module stays ignorant of what it built. All existing call sites construct positionally, so behavior is unchanged for them.

**Doc note (premises):** `Configure` is documented as THE sanctioned way a game teaches the palette to build its objects.

## 2. Undoable Restart

- New `Undo/RestartUndoCommand.cs` — holds the pre-restart `SceneData` snapshot; `Revert` restores it through the reader (the same sweep → `RebuildCodeContent` → `RestoreSnapshot` delegates a tab switch uses), `Apply` re-runs the teardown + reload-from-disk (redo).
- `EditorHistory.PushApplied` — records a command WITHOUT invoking `Apply` (the restart already ran); refused inside a coalescing transaction.
- `EditorTransport.Restart` captures the snapshot via the stack's existing `CaptureSnapshot` seam BEFORE `_history.Clear()`, and pushes the one surviving undo entry after the reload. Exactly one level deep; screens without the snapshot seams wired restart exactly as before (nothing pushed).

**Noted behavior (inherited from the reference, kept as-is):** with the seams wired, the dirty indicator lights immediately after a Restart — the pushed entry bumps the edit version past the save point. Flagging rather than silently deviating; `MarkSavePoint()` after the push would change it if we ever want "restart lands clean".

## 3. Two placement fixes

- The **active bottom tab joins the palette's layout cache key** (`_laidOutBottomTab`): a programmatic tab switch (the `panel:tab` op, a prefab flow) now re-lays the shelf chrome instead of leaving the Assets chrome painted over the Prefabs tab.
- **Drag-stamp duplicate guards**: a per-stroke visited set (a wobbling/back-tracking drag never doubles a cell — the old previous-position guard can't catch A→B→A revisits) plus a cross-stroke duplicate-cell guard (re-clicking a filled cell with the identical prop is a loud-logged no-op that costs no undo step).

## 4. Grid density fade

Zoomed out, the grid congealed into a solid wall of lines. Minors now fade in steps as their on-screen spacing shrinks (≥48px full → ≥24px 0.55× → ≥12px 0.3× → gone; majors carry the packed grid), from a quieter 0.55 base alpha. The fade is applied **premultiplied** — one deliberate deviation from the reference: it builds the faded color with raw `new Color(...)`, which this repo's `EditorThemeLintTests` forbids in level-editor sources; the identical arithmetic is expressed as `Color.Lerp(Color.Transparent, role, alpha)` (both tokens lint-blessed).

## Docs

`MonoDreams/level-editor/docs/premises.md` updated in the same PR: the seam note on the trigger premise, the restart-undo paragraph on the transport premise, the dedupe guards on the multi-stamp premise, the density fade on the grid premise, and a new layout-cache-key invariant on the palette-cards premise — each with the new tests wired into its `Tests:` field.
